tagline: Iowa to Canada on the old King of Trails.
intro: US 75 runs the whole length of Minnesota close to its western border, up from the Iowa line south of Luverne through Pipestone, Canby and Breckenridge to Moorhead, then northeast to Crookston and back northwest toward the Red River, to stop at the Canadian line at Noyes. It passes through few large towns.

Before the state numbered its trunk highways in 1920 the road was an auto trail called the King of Trails, and the towns along it have had the whole Minnesota stretch officially named the Historic King of Trails again.

moments.title: Pipestone National Monument
moments.text: Beside the highway north of Pipestone, the red stone has been quarried for ceremonial pipes for over 3,000 years, on ground once held neutral so every nation could dig.

moments.title: Breckenridge
moments.text: At Breckenridge and Wahpeton, its twin across the line in North Dakota, the Bois de Sioux and Otter Tail rivers join to make the Red River of the North.

moments.title: Noyes
moments.text: The highway ends at a border it can no longer cross, beside a 1931 customs station counted among the nation's first purpose-built land border checkpoints.
